decisions.quote: Such differences between willingness and comfort levels have become easier to see: in the 2017 study, willingness and comfort mirrored one another, while this study saw a distinct separation of the two when looking at the comfort of using telemedicine with a wholly new health care professional—18.6% for both comfort and willingness in 2017, and 33.49% comfort and 33.86% willingness now [ 14 ].
decisions.reason: The paper does not state an overall replication verdict for Welch et al. (2017) as a whole, so Rule 2 applies. In comparing the 2022 survey results to the 2017 baseline, the authors report that some findings held (e.g., general health care access was largely unchanged and willingness and comfort showed a similar decreasing trend as interpersonal distance from the patient's own PCP increased) while explicitly contrasting other results with 2017 (dramatically higher telemedicine awareness and use, as well as a separation between willingness and comfort where the 2017 study found they mirrored one another). Furthermore, the shipped outcome quote ('Telemedicine ease of use and satisfaction were comparable to in-person visits.') refers to new extension items added in 2022 rather than a comparison with the 2017 study. Because some explicit comparisons agree with the original and others explicitly contrast with it, the outcome is mixed.
